title: Pagination and filtering library
goal: All list endpoints share one cursor-pagination and filtering library that produces the CT-PAGE response shape, with opaque, filter-bound, expiring cursors.
scope_in: Query parsing: `limit` 1..200 (default 50), `cursor`, optional `sort` from an endpoint allow-list; invalid values give a validation problem with `errors[]` pointers.

Cursor codec: base64url of JSON `{v:1, k:<keyset values>, f:<filter hash>, s:<sort>, exp:<unix>}` plus HMAC-SHA256 signature (keys from config `CURSOR_SIGNING_KEYS`, newest signs, all verify); URL-safe; expires after 24 h; bound to the same filters and sort.

Kysely keyset helper `paginate(query, spec, params)` fetching `limit + 1` rows, building `(sort_col, id)` tuple comparisons for asc/desc, always tie-breaking on id; returns `{data, next_cursor, has_more}`.
Filter helper: declared filter fields with types (string, enum, id, timestamp range) parsed from query, unknown filters ignored, hashed into the cursor.
Response builder `page(data, next_cursor)` and Fastify decorator `reply.page(...)`; helper for in-memory arrays used by non-SQL lists.
scope_out: Endpoint-specific queries (each lane writes its list query using this library).
Sparse field selection `?fields=` (not supported in v1).
build_against: B010 test stack with a throwaway table of 1 000 rows; pure unit tests for the codec with a fake clock.
interfaces: `parsePageQuery(q: unknown, spec:{sorts: readonly string[]; defaultSort: string}): {limit: number; cursor?: string; sort: string}`.
`encodeCursor(payload: CursorPayload, keys: SigningKeys, now: number): string`; `decodeCursor(c: string, keys: SigningKeys, now: number, expect:{filterHash: string; sort: string}): CursorPayload`.
`paginate<DB, TB, O>(qb: SelectQueryBuilder<DB, TB, O>, spec: KeysetSpec, params: PageParams): Promise<Page<O>>` where `Page<T> = {data: T[]; next_cursor: string|null; has_more: boolean}`.
acceptance: Listing 1 000 rows with limit 200 returns 5 pages, `has_more` true on the first 4 and false on the last, `next_cursor` null on the last, with no row duplicated or skipped, in stable order.
Default limit is 50; `limit=0`, `limit=201`, `limit=abc` return a validation problem pointing at `/limit`.
Rows inserted between page fetches never cause duplicates or skips in the already-fetched ordering (keyset test with concurrent inserts).
Changing a filter or sort while reusing a cursor is rejected (filter-hash mismatch); a cursor older than 24 h (fake clock) is rejected; a cursor with one flipped byte is rejected.
Cursors cannot be forged without the key (HMAC checked in constant time) and carry no row data beyond keyset values.
Key rotation: a cursor signed with the previous key still verifies; an unknown key id is rejected.
Sorting by a non-unique column (created_at with 100 identical timestamps) is stable thanks to the id tie-breaker.
Generated SQL uses parameter placeholders only (query-log assertion) and EXPLAIN on a 100k-row table with a matching index shows no sequential scan.
tests: cursor.test.ts: codec, tamper, expiry, key rotation.
keyset.test.ts: asc/desc, ties, concurrent inserts on real Postgres.
filters.test.ts: hash stability and unknown filters.
plugin.test.ts and fuzz.test.ts: response shape, reply.page, decodeCursor never throws untyped errors.
guardrails: MUST NOT implement or accept offsets, page numbers or `skip`.
MUST sign cursors and bind them to filters and sort so a client cannot read other scopes by editing a cursor.
MUST NOT include secrets, emails or content in cursor payloads (keyset values only).
MUST always add the unique id as the final sort key; MUST NOT expose total counts.
MUST clamp `limit` server-side to 200 even if a caller passes a higher spec maximum.
failure_modes: Invalid/expired/tampered cursor -> 400-class validation problem on `/cursor`, never 500.
Signing key missing -> service refuses to start.
Empty result -> `{data: [], next_cursor: null, has_more: false}`.
notes: CONTRACT GAP: no dedicated error code exists for an expired/invalid cursor in the .md contracts; use the generic validation error until errors.json lists one. Adds no third-party dependency (node:crypto).
